title: Empire Swim Lanes
description: A swim-lane timeline of South Asia from 600 to 1800 CE with ten lanes: the Cholas, Sri Lankan kingdoms, the Delhi Sultanate, the Bengal Sultanate, the Vijayanagara Empire, the Deccan sultanates, the Mughal Empire, the Maratha Empire, the Durrani Empire and European trading companies. A moving year line shows which powers existed at the same time, and each bar opens a card with dates, capital and one key fact.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
World history
South Asia
Empires and kingdoms
Timelines
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Compare the approximate dates of major South Asian powers between 600 and 1800 CE.
Identify powers that existed at the same time in a chosen year.
Explain why history in this period is better pictured as overlapping lanes than as one empire replacing another.
prerequisites: Reading a timeline with years in CE
Chapter 2: Ancient Roots (the Maurya and Gupta empires)
keyQuestions: Which powers existed in South Asia in the year 1600?
Did each empire replace the one before it, or did they overlap?
When did European trading companies appear, and who else ruled at that time?
misconceptions: Each empire neatly replaced the one before it.
The Mughals ruled all of South Asia.
The East India Company was the British government.
controls: Click or tap a bar for its details
